newsitem.title: USA: NYC fails to collect welfare overpayments - watchdog.
newsitem.headline: NYC fails to collect welfare overpayments - watchdog.

text.p: A New York City watchdog Thursday faulted the Guiliani Administration for not getting welfare recipients to give back overpayments nearly 10 percent of the time, saying this cost the city millions of dollars.
In one case, a person got 34 rent overpayments that added up to more than $14,400, city comptroller Alan Hevesi said in the report.
And another got 21 rent overpayments that were worth $20,200, he said.

One of 40 centers, the Melrose income maintenance center in the Bronx, accounted for 48 out of the 90 sample cases, he added, noting that the Administration has promised to make make all the changes that are needed to correct the problem.
As only one overpayment can be collected at a time, some are not repaid for years.
"Because of poor procedures at the Human Resources Administration, the city was not collecting millions of dollars in extra rent payments owed to it by welfare recipients," the city comptroller said.

Although the city was owed $144.6 million from 77,118 closed cases as of April 1996, the city Human Resources Department was only able to collect $1.7 million in the first nine months of that fiscal year, the city comptroller said.
